posts.title: Utah Jazz Open Preseason With Win over Denver Nuggets: Three Takeaways
posts.author: Eric Spyropoulos
posts.summary: After a summer full of anticipation, Utah Jazz basketball made its return Sunday night.
facts: After a summer full of anticipation, Utah Jazz basketball made its return Sunday night.
Although it was only a preseason matchup against the Denver Nuggets, Jazz fans finally got to see the 2026-27 squad in action.
Utah fought through multiple cold spells offensively to gain control and pull out a 109-97 win to open the preseason slate of games.
The long ball was a key weapon for the Jazz (15 made threes), while an edge on the boards (63-55) also helped fuel the victory.
The Jazz closed the opening frame on a 19-6 run, fueled by good ball movement (11 assists in the quarter) and hot shooting (52 percent from the field and five made 3-pointers).
It was a similar story in the second quarter, as Utah shot 1-of-10 from the field to begin the frame before using regular trips to the free-throw line to find more of a rhythm on the offensive end.
Lauri Markkanen totaled 17 points in the first half, with Jaren Jackson Jr. (11 points) and Keyonte George (10 points) following The Finnisher’s lead.
On the defensive end, the Jazz forced six turnovers and limited Denver to 44 percent shooting from the field, which helped push the visitors in front 63-52.
